fields.description: Issue focuses on the upcoming Miami city commission primary election (Nov. 15, 1949) and Miami Life’s poll of candidates, with extensive editorial criticism of candidate Leonard K. Thomson’s record (utility tax, cigarette tax, garbage tax, stance on homestead exemption) and discussion of proposed consolidation of city and county tax assessor functions and its impact on residential vs. downtown commercial property taxes. Also reports on alleged influence of Cuban senator Jose Aleman in Miami and Washington, including immigration official transfers and a claimed congressional probe; includes coverage of Herald pressmen firings and union control, a petition challenging Southern Bell pay-phone practices, and local police/court and Orange Bowl incident reporting, plus candidate statements/advertising.
